name: IL-12
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strong R+22 partisan lean of IL-12
Incumbent Mike Bost running with a large financial edge ($1.3M raised vs $88K)
No polls or expert ratings; challenger is minimally funded
model.rationale: The district's R+22 lean, Bost's incumbency and overwhelming fundraising advantage, and markets pricing him near 97% all point to a safe Republican hold; the Democratic challenger has raised little and drawn no outside support.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending or an unexpected polling miss in downstate Illinois could narrow the margin, though a Bost loss remains unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview: Mike Bost, the Republican incumbent in southern Illinois's 12th District, seeks another term in a seat with a strong Republican lean of about 22 points. He enters the general election with a large financial advantage, having raised roughly $1.3 million and holding nearly $790,000 on hand, while Democrat Julie Fortier has raised under $90,000 with no meaningful outside support. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets give Bost about a 97 percent chance of winning. The fundamentals align: the district's lean, incumbency, and the money gap all favor the incumbent. The forecast expects Bost to win comfortably, with modest uncertainty reflecting the absence of polling in this low-attention race.
